sources_that_worked.note: Highest-value source in the run. The grantee search — not the model search — is what makes an absent grant interpretable.
Manufacturer spec tables state Wi-Fi/Bluetooth support explicitly. Vendor knowledge-base blog posts carry the firmware procedure.
Specialist retailer support desk. Good Class B for 'does this vendor operate a cloud at all' questions.

sources_that_failed.error: Article page lists PDF links only; content not inline

rules_added: PRINCIPLES §3 — an absent FCC grant is only evidence with the sibling-model control; search the grantee, not the model.
VERIFIER step 4 — radios are not cloud. Name the vendor's cloud endpoint before assigning D2, or it is probably D1.
VERIFIER step 1 — manual-aggregator sites 403 automated fetches; go to the manufacturer domain or search the specific procedure.
surprises: The D1/D2 boundary turned out to be the interesting one, not D0/D1. The A139 has Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and a phone app, and is still D1 — VIOFO runs no cloud service whatsoever, so the app is peer-to-peer to the camera's own AP. An agent pattern-matching on 'has Wi-Fi and an app' would have called it D2 and been wrong. Also worth noting: VIOFO sells radio-free and radio-equipped models side by side in the same product line, which is what makes their FCC filing history such a clean control group. Look for other vendors with that shape.
